# --description--

Optional chaining shines when data may be missing at several levels: an object can be `nil`, and one of its properties can be `nil` too.
A single `?.` chain handles both cases without any `if`.

# --instructions--

Write a function `authorName` with the parameter `of` of type `Book?` that returns the book's `author`, or `"Unknown"` when the book or its author is missing.
Keep the `Book` class as it is

# --before-seed--

```swift
// DO NOT EDIT FROM HERE
import Foundation

var _testCount = 0
var _testFailedCount = 0
func tryCatch(_ assertion: Bool) {
    _testCount += 1
    if !assertion {
        _testFailedCount += 1
        print("Test Case '--err-t\(_testCount)--' failed")
    }
}
// DO NOT EDIT UNTIL HERE
```

# --seed--

```swift
class Book {
    var author: String?
}
```

# --asserts--

A book whose author is `"Ada"` must return `"Ada"`

```swift
let novel = Book()
novel.author = "Ada"
tryCatch(authorName(of: novel) == "Ada")
```

A book without an author must return `"Unknown"`

```swift
tryCatch(authorName(of: Book()) == "Unknown")
```

A `nil` book must return `"Unknown"`

```swift
tryCatch(authorName(of: nil) == "Unknown")
```

# --after-asserts--

```swift
print("Executed \(_testCount) tests, with \(_testFailedCount) failures")
```

# --solutions--

```swift
class Book {
    var author: String?
}
func authorName(of book: Book?) -> String {
    return book?.author ?? "Unknown"
}
```
